{"type":"text","timestamp":1793011663058,"sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","part":{"id":"prt_177d2be50001Ya8g9gtmvbiEbR","messageID":"msg_177d2b5a6001nu2x1ZjofFdSgU","sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","type":"text","text":"The original builds, passes validation, and uses FMA contraction (`vfmadd`), so a GPU kernel using explicit FMA in the same k order should reproduce its C bit-for-bit. I'll use the printed hash as the check.\n\nPlan:\n- **MPI**: one row block per rank, sized by the number of GPUs each rank owns. Rank 0 gathers C with `MPI_Gatherv`. Inputs are generated deterministically on every rank, so no input broadcast is needed.\n- **OpenMP**: one host thread per local GPU drives that device; also used for parallel matrix initialization.\n- **CUDA**: a shared-memory tiled double-precision kernel that keeps k sequential per element, so results match the original exactly. I'm not using cuBLAS, since it would change summation order.\n\nWriting the new source now.","time":{"start":1793011662416,"end":1793011663051}}}
{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793011681021,"sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01DzHj8fZnFcEaz3mJZ9VDa2","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/matmul/matmul.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Abort the whole MPI job on any CUDA runtime error (avoids hangs in collectives).\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                                 \\\n    do {                                                                                 \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                       \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                       \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,             \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                           \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                                \\\n        }                                                                                \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Generate pseudo-random values for matrix initialization\nconstexpr double getPseudoRndValue(const size_t N, const size_t i, const size_t j) noexcept {\n    return (((i + 1) * (i + j + 1) * 1299709) % (N * N)) / static_cast<double>(N * N);\n}\n\n// Host-parallel (OpenMP) initialization; each element is independent.\nvoid initMatrix(std::vector<double>& mat, const size_t N, const int threads) {\n#pragma omp parallel for num_threads(threads) schedule(static)\n    for (long long i = 0; i < static_cast<long long>(N); ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            mat[static_cast<size_t>(i) * N + j] = getPseudoRndValue(N, static_cast<size_t>(i), j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// CUDA kernel: C[rows x N] = A[rows x N] * B[N x N], row-major, double precision.\n//\n// Shared-memory tiling with 4x4 register micro-tiles per thread. Every output\n// element accumulates its k-terms strictly in ascending order with a fused\n// multiply-add, which is the same arithmetic order and rounding as the original\n// sequential triple loop, so results are bit-identical.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nconstexpr int TILE_M = 64;\nconstexpr int TILE_N = 64;\nconstexpr int TILE_K = 16;\nconstexpr int THREAD_M = 4;\nconstexpr int THREAD_N = 4;\nconstexpr int BLOCK_X = TILE_N / THREAD_N;  // 16\nconstexpr int BLOCK_Y = TILE_M / THREAD_M;  // 16\nconstexpr int NTHREADS = BLOCK_X * BLOCK_Y; // 256\n\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(NTHREADS)\nmatmulKernel(const double* __restrict__ A, const double* __restrict__ B,\n             double* __restrict__ C, const size_t rows, const size_t N) {\n    __shared__ double As[TILE_M][TILE_K + 1];\n    __shared__ double Bs[TILE_K][TILE_N + 1];\n\n    const int tid = threadIdx.y * BLOCK_X + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t rowBase = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * TILE_M;\n    const size_t colBase = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * TILE_N;\n\n    double acc[THREAD_M][THREAD_N];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int m = 0; m < THREAD_M; ++m)\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int n = 0; n < THREAD_N; ++n) acc[m][n] = 0.0;\n\n    for (size_t k0 = 0; k0 < N; k0 += TILE_K) {\n        for (int t = tid; t < TILE_M * TILE_K; t += NTHREADS) {\n            const int r = t / TILE_K;\n            const int c = t % TILE_K;\n            const size_t gr = rowBase + r;\n            const size_t gk = k0 + c;\n            As[r][c] = (gr < rows && gk < N) ? A[gr * N + gk] : 0.0;\n        }\n        for (int t = tid; t < TILE_K * TILE_N; t += NTHREADS) {\n            const int r = t / TILE_N;\n            const int c = t % TILE_N;\n            const size_t gk = k0 + r;\n            const size_t gc = colBase + c;\n            Bs[r][c] = (gk < N && gc < N) ? B[gk * N + gc] : 0.0;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        const size_t remaining = N - k0;\n        const int kmax = remaining < static_cast<size_t>(TILE_K) ? static_cast<int>(remaining) : TILE_K;\n        for (int kk = 0; kk < kmax; ++kk) {\n            double a[THREAD_M];\n            double b[THREAD_N];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int m = 0; m < THREAD_M; ++m) a[m] = As[threadIdx.y * THREAD_M + m][kk];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int n = 0; n < THREAD_N; ++n) b[n] = Bs[kk][threadIdx.x * THREAD_N + n];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int m = 0; m < THREAD_M; ++m)\n#pragma unroll\n                for (int n = 0; n < THREAD_N; ++n) acc[m][n] = __fma_rn(a[m], b[n], acc[m][n]);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int m = 0; m < THREAD_M; ++m) {\n        const size_t gr = rowBase + threadIdx.y * THREAD_M + m;\n        if (gr >= rows) continue;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int n = 0; n < THREAD_N; ++n) {\n            const size_t gc = colBase + threadIdx.x * THREAD_N + n;\n            if (gc < N) C[gr * N + gc] = acc[m][n];\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Multiply a block of `rows` rows of A (full B) on one GPU; result written to hC.\nvoid multiplyOnDevice(const int device, const double* hA, const double* hB, double* hC,\n                      const size_t rows, const size_t N) {\n    if (rows == 0 || N == 0) return;\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(device));\n\n    const size_t aBytes = rows * N * sizeof(double);\n    const size_t bBytes = N * N * sizeof(double);\n\n    double *dA = nullptr, *dB = nullptr, *dC = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dA, aBytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dB, bBytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dC, aBytes));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dA, hA, aBytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dB, hB, bBytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    const dim3 block(BLOCK_X, BLOCK_Y);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned int>((N + TILE_N - 1) / TILE_N),\n                    static_cast<unsigned int>((rows + TILE_M - 1) / TILE_M));\n    matmulKernel<<<grid, block>>>(dA, dB, dC, rows, N);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    // Synchronous D2H copy also waits for the kernel to finish.\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(hC, dC, aBytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dA));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dB));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dC));\n}\n\n// Simple validation: compute a single element and compare\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& A, const std::vector<double>& B,\n                   const std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    // Check a few random positions\n    constexpr size_t checkPoints[] = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4};\n    \n    for (size_t pi = 0; pi < 5; ++pi) {\n        for (size_t pj = 0; pj < 5; ++pj) {\n            const size_t i = checkPoints[pi] % N;\n            const size_t j = checkPoints[pj] % N;\n            \n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += A[i * N + k] * B[k * N + j];\n            }\n            \n            const double actual = C[i * N + j];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actual - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n            \n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, j, expected, actual, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size N (computes NxN * NxN) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int worldRank = 0;\n    int worldSize = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &worldRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &worldSize);\n\n    size_t N = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    bool exitEarly = false;\n    int exitCode = 0;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            N = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (worldRank == 0) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            exitEarly = true;\n            break;\n        } else {\n            if (worldRank == 0) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            exitCode = 1;\n            exitEarly = true;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (exitEarly) {\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return exitCode;\n    }\n    \n    if (worldRank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Matrix Multiplication Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", N, N);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // ---- Topology: local (shared-memory) ranks and GPU assignment ----\n    MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, worldRank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    int localSize = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(localComm, &localSize);\n\n    int numDevices = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&numDevices));\n    if (numDevices == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"No CUDA devices available\\n\");\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n\n    // Each local rank drives a set of GPUs. If there are at least as many ranks as GPUs,\n    // ranks share GPUs round-robin; otherwise GPUs are partitioned among local ranks.\n    std::vector<int> myDevices;\n    if (localSize >= numDevices) {\n        myDevices.push_back(localRank % numDevices);\n    } else {\n        for (int d = 0; d < numDevices; ++d) {\n            if (d % localSize == localRank) myDevices.push_back(d);\n        }\n    }\n    const int myDevCount = static_cast<int>(myDevices.size());\n\n    // Row partition across ranks, weighted by the number of GPUs each rank drives.\n    std::vector<int> devCounts(worldSize);\n    MPI_Allgather(&myDevCount, 1, MPI_INT, devCounts.data(), 1, MPI_INT, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    size_t totalWeight = 0;\n    for (int r = 0; r < worldSize; ++r) totalWeight += static_cast<size_t>(devCounts[r]);\n    std::vector<size_t> rowBounds(worldSize + 1, 0);\n    {\n        size_t prefix = 0;\n        for (int r = 0; r < worldSize; ++r) {\n            prefix += static_cast<size_t>(devCounts[r]);\n            rowBounds[r + 1] = N * prefix / totalWeight;\n        }\n    }\n    const size_t myRowBegin = rowBounds[worldRank];\n    const size_t myRows = rowBounds[worldRank + 1] - myRowBegin;\n\n    // Host threads: share the node's cores among local ranks.\n    const int hostThreads = std::max(1, omp_get_num_procs() / localSize);\n\n    // Allocate matrices (every rank deterministically generates the full inputs,\n    // so no input communication is needed).\n    std::vector<double> A(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> B(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> C(N * N);\n\n    if (worldRank == 0) printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    initMatrix(A, N, hostThreads);\n    initMatrix(B, N, hostThreads);\n\n    // Create CUDA contexts before timing so context setup is not measured.\n#pragma omp parallel for num_threads(myDevCount) schedule(static, 1)\n    for (int t = 0; t < myDevCount; ++t) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(myDevices[t]));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(nullptr));\n    }\n\n    // Perform matrix multiplication\n    if (worldRank == 0) printf(\"Computing matrix multiplication...\\n\");\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    // Each local GPU computes a contiguous sub-block of this rank's rows.\n#pragma omp parallel for num_threads(myDevCount) schedule(static, 1)\n    for (int t = 0; t < myDevCount; ++t) {\n        const size_t g0 = myRowBegin + myRows * static_cast<size_t>(t) / myDevCount;\n        const size_t g1 = myRowBegin + myRows * static_cast<size_t>(t + 1) / myDevCount;\n        multiplyOnDevice(myDevices[t], A.data() + g0 * N, B.data(), C.data() + g0 * N, g1 - g0, N);\n    }\n\n    // Gather the full C on rank 0 (row blocks are contiguous and ordered by rank).\n    MPI_Datatype rowType;\n    MPI_Type_contiguous(static_cast<int>(N), MPI_DOUBLE, &rowType);\n    MPI_Type_commit(&rowType);\n    std::vector<int> counts(worldSize);\n    std::vector<int> displs(worldSize);\n    for (int r = 0; r < worldSize; ++r) {\n        counts[r] = static_cast<int>(rowBounds[r + 1] - rowBounds[r]);\n        displs[r] = static_cast<int>(rowBounds[r]);\n    }\n    if (worldRank == 0) {\n        MPI_Gatherv(MPI_IN_PLACE, 0, rowType, C.data(), counts.data(), displs.data(), rowType,\n                    0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    } else {\n        MPI_Gatherv(C.data() + myRowBegin * N, counts[worldRank], rowType, nullptr,\n                    counts.data(), displs.data(), rowType, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    }\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    if (worldRank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n        // Calculate GFLOPS\n        double gflops = (2.0 * N * N * N) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n        // Print results for external validation\n        if (printResults) {\n            print_results(C, \"MatrixC\");\n        }\n\n        // Validation\n        if (validate) {\n            printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n            bool valid = validateResult(A, B, C, N);\n\n            if (valid) {\n                printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            } else {\n                printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n                exitCode = 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    MPI_Type_free(&rowType);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&localComm);\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return exitCode;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/matmul/matmul.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/matmul/matmul.cpp","time":{"start":1793011680932,"end":1793011680987}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_177d2c0cf001I0kK8OOErDnx31","sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","messageID":"msg_177d2b5a6001nu2x1ZjofFdSgU"}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793011685126,"sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01EXfrEcHFUesrfe2F5YxeFM","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","content":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(matmul_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\n# Default GPU targets: Ampere (A100, RTX 30xx), Hopper (H100). Override with -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=...\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 80 86 90)\nendif()\n\nfind_package(MPI REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(OpenMP REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\n# matmul.cpp contains the CUDA kernel and is compiled by nvcc; host code is passed to the host compiler.\nset_source_files_properties(matmul.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\n\nadd_executable(matmul matmul.cpp)\n\ntarget_compile_options(matmul PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-march=native,-Wall,-Wextra,-fopenmp>\n)\n\ntarget_link_libraries(matmul PRIVATE\n    MPI::MPI_CXX\n    OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX\n    CUDA::cudart\n    m\n)\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","time":{"start":1793011685085,"end":1793011685095}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_177d311f90013FTNmvxso3PjtI","sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","messageID":"msg_177d306ef001nv3cS9QrNZlyAk"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793011832060,"sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","part":{"id":"prt_177d51dd5001y1XxdKfE4ALka6","messageID":"msg_177d51a4d001Nsc64wBSOYa359","sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm noticing GCC actually vectorizes pairs of k values, computing two products with vmulpd but still combining them in strict sequential order using vaddsd, preserving the original floating-point addition order without needing -ffast-math.\n\nSo the only FMA in the loop is for the trailing odd element when N is odd — meaning for even N there's no fusion, but for odd N the last term gets fused. That means bit-exact reproduction on GPU requires disabling FMA contraction (like nvcc's -fmad=false or explicit __dmul_rn/__dadd_rn calls) for the regular terms, while still matching the compiler's parity-dependent fusing behavior for the tail element — which is a tricky, compiler-specific detail to replicate exactly.\n\nGiven the 1e-6 validation tolerance, I suspect this exactness isn't actually required and I'm overthinking a compiler artifact; the real test likely just checks the hash against a default N (probably even, like 512) where no FMA occurs in the original. I'll verify this by testing small odd/even N cases to confirm where the divergence actually matters before deciding how closely to emulate it.\n\nMatching the built binary bit-for-bit across N seems like the most defensible notion of equivalent semantics here, since the odd-N fused tail is a stable artifact of this specific compiler and build configuration. I'll implement the non-fused main loop with a fused final term for odd N, document it as reproducing the compiler's contraction behavior, and verify empirically by probing N=301.\n\nFor the kernel, I'm tracking the global k index and fusing only the last term when N is odd, branching minimally to avoid divergence costs. But this raises a real performance tradeoff: using separate dmul+dadd instead of a single fma roughly doubles the instruction cost on the FP64 pipe, so matching bit-exactness with the original sacrifices throughput versus a fully-fused \"maximum performance\" version.\n\nI'm deciding to prioritize exact equivalence with the original's hash and semantics, since correctness checking matters more than raw speed here, and I'll note the performance tradeoff explicitly. Still working out how to detect whether the last tile contains index N-1 to apply fusion there...\n\nWriting the loop logic...\n\nI also confirm the host-side validation path is untouched and will behave identically to the original, so I'm ready to finalize the kernel edit.\n\n","time":{"start":1793011817941,"end":1793011832020},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793011832061,"sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","part":{"id":"prt_177d554db0017SB01R0RKgMO2F","messageID":"msg_177d51a4d001Nsc64wBSOYa359","sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","type":"text","text":"This resolves the contradiction. GCC vectorized the k-loop: it computes products two at a time with `vmulpd`, but adds them in strict sequential order with separate `vaddsd`, so the main loop is **not** fused. Only the scalar tail (the final term when N is odd) is contracted into `vfmadd`. So the original's result is: separate multiply-add for every k, except the last term when N is odd.\n\nMy kernel used FMA everywhere, which is why the hash differs. I'll match the original exactly: use separate rounded multiply and add (`__dmul_rn`/`__dadd_rn`, which nvcc never contracts), and fuse only the final k-term when N is odd. This costs FP64 throughput on the 3090, so I'll note it in the summary. Making that edit now.","time":{"start":1793011832027,"end":1793011832049}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793012277973,"sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","part":{"id":"prt_177dc050c0014NYkGhOz8ujBLG","messageID":"msg_177dc007b001OQyfp9pkRB7GLs","sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm noticing the scaling from 1 to 4 ranks looks weak, only going from 806 to 902 GFLOPS instead of roughly 4x — likely because np=1 already spans all 4 GPUs via threads, so the baseline is already using full hardware and the per-GPU throughput seems low for fp64.\n\nWorking through the peak estimate: with non-fused multiply-add, the 3090's effective FP64 ceiling is about 278 GFLOPS per GPU, or roughly 1100 across four GPUs — and the measured 806-900 is actually quite close to that, which makes sense given the bit-exact constraint ruling out fused ops. The other smaller checks (help flag exit codes, unknown option errors, small-N timing) all look fine. I also want to look at whether memory transfer time is eating into the larger N=8192 run, since the host-to-device copy could account for a meaningful chunk of the total time and pinned memory might help.\n\nRegistering A and B with cudaHostRegister once per rank before timing starts seems like a cheap way to speed up the async copies without affecting correctness, since host registration is process-wide and should work fine across multiple devices per rank. I want to just try it and measure N=8192 with a single rank against the noisy ~1364ms baseline to see if it actually helps before committing to the change.\n\n","time":{"start":1793012270348,"end":1793012277912},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793012277974,"sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","part":{"id":"prt_177dc229b0019xdzL1fWh52mRT","messageID":"msg_177dc007b001OQyfp9pkRB7GLs","sessionID":"ses_e882f1661ffejpH1yzG48UU9F5","type":"text","text":"Results:\n- **Correctness**: all sizes match the original, and the `-h`/unknown-option paths behave correctly. The non-zero exit for `-x` is expected.\n- **Performance**: 806 GFLOPS at N=8192 on 4 GPUs. The 3090's FP64 peak is about 556 GFLOPS per GPU with FMA, and separate multiply and add halves that, so the ceiling for bit-exact mode is roughly 1100 GFLOPS. I'm at about 75-80% of it.\n\nOne cheap improvement remains: host-to-device copies from pageable memory are slow. I'll try pinning the rank's A and B buffers (registered once, outside timing) and measure whether it helps.","time":{"start":1793012277915,"end":1793012277933}}}

The fix is to set CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES before the `project()` call, so it's established as a normal variable before CMake's CUDA detection populates the cache — this is the documented pattern, and user-supplied `-D` overrides still work fine. CUDA 12.0's nvcc supports compute_80/86/90 without issue, so I'll apply this fix and rebuild.\n\n","time":{"start":1793012503087,"end":1793012507675},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

LANGUAGES CUDA)` initializes the cache variable `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` to nvcc's default (52) before my `if(NOT DEFINED ...)` runs, so the default never applies.
